sources.title: Vladimir Ivanov and Grigori Olshanski, Kerov's central limit theorem for the Plancherel measure on Young diagrams, arXiv:math/0304010; survey-paper version in Symmetric Functions 2001, NATO Science Series II 74 (2002), 93-151
sources.locator: §§ 2-6, printed pp. 9-33: continual diagrams and moment functionals (§2), the elements p_k^# (§3), the basis {p_rho^#} and filtrations (§4, including Corollary 4.8 of Proposition 4.7's proof, p. 22), the Plancherel measure and law of large numbers (§5), the central limit theorem for characters (§6); §7 (printed pp. 33-38) inspected for the boundary disposition only. The proof texts of Props. 2.2, 2.11, 3.4-3.7, 4.2, 4.5, 4.7, Cor. 4.8, 4.9-4.13, 5.1-5.3, Thms. 5.4, 5.5, 6.1 and Lemmas 5.6-5.7 were read in full.

contents.name: §2 Defs. 2.1, 2.3 and 2.9-2.10 with Props. 2.2 and 2.11: continual diagrams, sigma=(omega-|x|)/2, the moment functionals tilde p_k, the scaling omega_s(x)=s^-1 omega(sx) and tilde p_k[omega_s]=s^-k tilde p_k[omega]
contents.proof_mapping: The rotation, support, scaling and area conventions are transcribed; the scaling identity of Prop. 2.11 is recorded as part (c) of the observables item.

contents.name: §3 Def. 3.1 and Props. 3.4-3.7: the functions p_k^#, their top canonical component p_k, the top weight component and the inversion formula expressing tilde p_k through the p_{j-1}^#
contents.proof_mapping: The inversion formula (source Prop. 3.7) is the change-of-basis statement proved in this lemma; the source proof (Lagrange inversion, Props. 3.5-3.6) is reproduced in authoring.

contents.name: §4 Def. 4.1, Props. 4.2, 4.5, 4.7, 4.9-4.13: definition of p_rho^# by shifted characters, membership in A and basis, structure constants via the partial-permutation algebra, the Kerov filtration, and the exact products with p_1^# and p_k^#
contents.proof_mapping: The structure constants, basis, and filtrations are carried by the theorem; Props. 4.11-4.12 exact product formulas are separated into lem-shifted-character-multiplication-by-p-k, and the Cor. 4.8 equality criterion used there is listed as a separate result below.

contents.name: §4 Corollary 4.8 (of the proof of Proposition 4.7): if f^rho_{sigma,tau} != 0 and deg_J(p_rho^#)=deg_J(p_sigma^#)+deg_J(p_tau^#), then B_J(s_1)=B_J(s_2)=empty and |B_J(s)|=|X_1 intersection X_2|
contents.proof_mapping: Fact F2 and step 1.2 of this item use the criterion with J={1}: it excludes fixed points of s_1 and s_2 in the overlap and, with the IK Prop. 6.2 partial-permutation count, gives the exact common-cycle alternatives for the top deg_1 term.

contents.name: §5 the Plancherel measure M_n(lambda)=dim^2 lambda/n!, Burnside normalization, Props. 5.1-5.3, Thm. 5.4 (law of large numbers, moment form), Lemma 5.6 (profile localization, citing Hammersley), Lemma 5.7 (weak versus uniform topology) and Thm. 5.5 (law of large numbers, sup form)
contents.proof_mapping: The measure is def-plancherel-measure-on-partitions; Prop. 5.1 is prop-plancherel-expectations-of-shifted-character-observables; Props. 5.2-5.3 feed prop-limit-profile-moments-are-central-binomial-coefficients; Thm. 5.4 is prop-scaled-plancherel-profile-moments-converge-in-probability; Lemma 5.7 is lem-bounded-lipschitz-profile-moments-control-uniform-distance; Lemma 5.6's Hammersley citation is replaced by the local RSK union bound lem-rsk-union-bound-localizes-plancherel-profiles.

contents.name: §6 Thm. 6.1 (character central limit theorem) with Props. 6.2-6.4: the extension by (p_1^#)^{1/2}, the Hermite leading terms eta_rho=prod H_{m_k}(eta_k)+negative-degree remainder, the moment method and the multivariate moment-determinacy criterion
contents.proof_mapping: Prop. 6.3 is lem-hermite-leading-terms-for-normalized-shifted-characters (in the concrete evaluation of the localization); the normalization eta_rho is def-normalized-shifted-character-basis-elements; Prop. 6.4 is thm-multivariate-method-of-moments-for-a-determinate-limit with the Gaussian determinacy supplied by lem-standard-gaussian-is-determined-by-its-moments; Thm. 6.1 is thm-kerov-central-limit-theorem-for-normalized-cycle-characters.

contents.name: §7 the central limit theorem for Young diagrams (Thm. 7.1: the centered profile fluctuation has Chebyshev-coordinate limit xi_{k+1}/sqrt(k+1)), §8-9 further applications (spectral measure of the Plancherel ensemble, Vershik-Kerov limit results)
contents.reason: The pair's promised claims end at the character CLT; the second-order diagram fluctuation theorem requires the additional moment-map inversion of §7 (Props. 7.3-7.4) and the spectral-measure applications of §8-9 are not part of this A page, which has no consumer for them.

sources.title: Vladimir Ivanov and Sergei Kerov, The algebra of conjugacy classes in symmetric groups and partial permutations, arXiv:math/0302203 <https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0302203>
sources.locator: §§ 6 and 9, printed pp. 5-7 and 12-13: the partial-permutation algebra A_infty, its structure constants, the support-union count, the equality case, and the isomorphism theorem; §§ 2-5 and 10-12 inspected for the transport conventions.

contents.name: Props. 6.1-6.3: A_sigma A_tau = sum g^rho_{sigma,tau} A_rho, the combinatorial count |G^rho_{sigma,tau}(n)| = g^rho_{sigma,tau}, and |rho| <= |sigma|+|tau| whenever g^rho_{sigma,tau} is nonzero
contents.proof_mapping: The count and the degree inequality are steps (1)-(2) of the proof strategy; the source proofs were read in full.

contents.name: Remark 6.4: the unique top partition rho=sigma union tau with g^{sigma union tau}_{sigma,tau} = prod_k binom(m_k(sigma)+m_k(tau), m_k(sigma))
contents.proof_mapping: The binomial product is exactly cancelled by the z-factors of the next row, giving coefficient 1 in the p^#-basis.

contents.name: Thm. 9.1 with the character evaluation (4.3)-(9.3): F(A_rho)=p_rho^#/z_rho is an isomorphism of algebras A_infty -> Lambda*
contents.proof_mapping: This is the transport map of step (3); the central-character evaluation is reproduced in authoring.

contents.name: §§ 2-5 and 10-12: partial permutations, the convolutions of conjugacy classes, and further identities in A_infty
contents.reason: Only the structure constants of §6, the equality case of Remark 6.4 and the isomorphism of Thm. 9.1 are used by this page; the remaining identities in A_infty have no consumer in the Plancherel pair.

sources.title: Dan Romik, The Surprising Mathematics of Longest Increasing Subsequences, Cambridge University Press 2015; author-hosted manuscript of 20 August 2014 (363 pp.)
sources.locator: §§ 1.6-1.8, printed pp. 17-28; §1.9, printed pp. 25-30; §§1.11-1.17, printed pp. 31-62; §1.20, printed pp. 68-69. The full 363-page manuscript was retrieved; the chapters beyond Chapter 1 were inspected for the boundary dispositions below.

contents.name: §1.8 Plancherel measure M_n(lambda)=dim(lambda)^2/n! and the Burnside sum of squares; the measure is introduced as the distribution of the RSK shape
contents.proof_mapping: The definition and normalization interface; the sum-of-squares identity is proved independently by prop-plancherel-weights-sum-to-one.

contents.name: §1.6-§1.7 the Robinson-Schensted algorithm and Young tableaux; §1.8 the shape of a uniform permutation is Plancherel-distributed
contents.proof_mapping: Independent book treatment of the counting argument used in the theorem.

contents.name: §1.9 the hook-length formula (Frame-Robinson-Thrall) with the deletion recursion
§1.10 an algorithm for sampling random standard Young tableaux (hook walk)
contents.reason: The hook walk is a sampling algorithm, not part of the promised limit-shape and CLT claims; no item on this page states or uses it.

contents.name: §§1.11-1.17 the limit shape theorem via the variational problem for hook integrals: asymptotic hook-length formula, transformation to hook coordinates, analysis of the functional, computation of J(h_0), and the first form of the limit shape theorem
contents.proof_mapping: This is the independent book treatment of the same limit-shape statement; the page proves the theorem by the Ivanov-Olshanski moment method, and Romik's variational route is recorded as the second, independent treatment (locator only, not reproduced).

contents.name: §1.18-§1.19 irreducible representations of S_n with maximal dimension and the Plancherel growth process; §1.20 the final version of the limit shape theorem
contents.reason: The growth process and the maximal-dimension computation are neighbours of the limit shape but are not among the pair's promised claims; the final form of the limit shape is the same statement already included.

contents.name: Chapter 2 (Baik-Deift-Johansson, Airy ensemble, Poissonized Plancherel measure, discrete Bessel kernel) and Chapters 3-5 (Erdos-Szekeres permutations, corner growth): Tracy-Widom and edge statistics
contents.reason: Fluctuation and edge theory of Plancherel measure belongs to analytic/integrable-probability suppliers and to RG-11's longest-increasing-subsequence development; this page proves only the law of large numbers and the character CLT.

sources.title: Piotr Sniady, Gaussian fluctuations of characters of symmetric groups and of Young diagrams, arXiv:math/0501112
sources.locator: §§ 1-3, printed pp. 1-16, in particular Theorem and Definition 3.1, Corollary 3.3, and the paragraph after (3.6) where the Plancherel case is recovered; §§ 4-5 inspected for the boundary disposition.

contents.name: Theorem and Definition 3.1 with Cor. 3.3: for representations with the character factorization property, the joint laws of q^{(|sigma_i|+1)/2}(chi^lambda(sigma_i)-E chi^lambda(sigma_i)) over cycles sigma_i are asymptotically Gaussian
contents.proof_mapping: Independent genus-expansion treatment of the same finite-dimensional Gaussian limit; the paragraph after (3.6) states that the Plancherel case recovers Kerov's central limit theorem. Used as the second, independent corroboration of the CLT claim.

contents.name: §§ 1-2: normalized conjugacy-class indicators, disjoint products, cumulants, transition measures and generalized Young diagrams
contents.reason: The cumulant and transition-measure language is specific to Sniady's genus-expansion proof method; the page follows the Hermite/moment-method proof of Ivanov-Olshanski and does not import this machinery.

contents.name: §§ 4-5: proofs by genus expansion, annular non-crossing partitions and the technical estimates
contents.reason: Proof machinery of the alternative route only; no statement in the page consumes the genus expansion or the non-crossing-partition combinatorics.

canonical.name: Shifted-character proof route of the limit-shape and character-CLT theorems, with the local RSK union bound replacing the source's Hammersley citation
Standard Stein-identity proof that the standard Gaussian is moment-determinate (the source's Proposition 6.4 assumes this)

sources.title: Dan Romik, The Surprising Mathematics of Longest Increasing Subsequences, Cambridge University Press 2015; author-hosted manuscript of 20 August 2014 (363 pp.)
sources.locator: §§1.6-1.9, printed pp. 17-30: RSK shapes, Plancherel weights, hook-length formula and the smallest dimensions.

contents.name: §1.6-§1.8 row insertion, the RSK shape law and the Plancherel weights dim(lambda)^2/n!
contents.proof_mapping: The six permutations of S_3 are inserted explicitly and their shape frequencies compared with the Plancherel weights; the weights dim^2/n! also exhibit non-uniformity at n=3.

contents.name: §1.9 the hook-length formula and the explicit dimensions f^(3)=f^(1^3)=1, f^(2,1)=2

sources.locator: §5, printed p. 25: the definition M_n(lambda)=dim^2 lambda/n! and the Burnside normalization, specialized at n=3.

contents.name: §5 the weights dim(lambda)^2/n! are shape-dependent, so the Plancherel measure is not the uniform measure on partitions
contents.proof_mapping: Specializing the source's definition to n=3 gives 1/6, 4/6, 1/6 against the uniform 1/3, 1/3, 1/3.

contents.name: §5 the definition and normalization of M_n for general n
